ny_wallface.blurb: Wallface is the big cliff above Indian Pass in the High Peaks of the Adirondacks, usually put at 700 to 800 feet tall and the largest wall in the park. It holds about a dozen climbs, mostly long traditional lines with a pair of aid routes and a lone bolted one. Grades run from easy fifth class through the 5.11 range, with the bulk of them between 5.9 and 5.11. The rock can be loose, the lines are committing, and a helmet matters. It is remote: expect roughly six miles in from the Loj on the Indian Pass Trail, then a bushwhack to reach the base. Few parties go, so solitude is the norm.

ny_snake_hole_left.blurb: Snake Hole Left is a small bouldering zone on the lower tier of The Loop at Powerlinez, about a dozen problems in all. It is the first boulder you meet when you drop down the little trail past the neighbouring sectors, with a big shelf on its left side overhanging a shallow cave. Problems range from an easy V0 up to one V10 outlier, but the core sits between V3 and V5, with a few V6-level lines nearby, so it suits climbers already comfortable on mid-grade boulders. Expect a quiet, compact spot reached by a steady uphill hike from the trailhead.

ny_phoenicia_sportsman_s_wall.blurb: Sportsman's Wall is a small bolted crag in the forest above the village of Phoenicia in the Catskills, an old abandoned quarry face. Roughly nine sport routes and a few boulder problems are scattered along it, from around 5.7 up through 5.11 and into the low 5.12 range, with most of the sport lines in the 5.10 to 5.11 bracket. Styles vary from short roofs to slopey faces, some holds are crumbly, and many of the bolts are painted to blend in. Allow about fifteen minutes on foot from town. Anchors are at the tops and often need threading, so bring a couple of spare carabiners.

ny_2_1_monkey_bar.blurb: Monkey Bar is a short, steep sector on the east end of Powerlinez that sits somewhere between a bouldering wall and a top-rope crag. Of its dozen lines, nearly all are top-rope problems with a single boulder problem. The routes are brief but full of dynamic, jungle-gym style moves, mostly in the 5.8 to 5.10 range with a couple of easier options. Because the lines are packed close together, several can be rigged from one tree anchor above the cliff. Reach that anchor by scrambling up around the west side of the left section.

ny_j_scrotum_pole_drive_in_area.blurb: This sector at Peterskill, the small conglomerate cliff in the Shawangunks, is centered on a narrow detached pillar with a slabby seating area just to its left. A dozen routes split evenly between top-rope and trad lines, running from 5.4 up to a 5.11 top-rope, with the bulk around 5.8 and 5.9. The setting is shaded but open, which makes it a comfortable choice for summer days, and it is popular with guides and groups. Walk in along a carriage road through a field, past a stream and a clearing, then up a footpath toward the amphitheater at the base.

ny_sharp_bridge_campground.blurb: Sharp Bridge is a small traditional crag in the Adirondacks near North Hudson, close to Northway Exit 30. The dozen routes are all trad, with a little top-roping, and the grades are friendly: easy fifth class through the 5.7 to 5.9 range, topping out around 5.10. The rock is clean, fine-grained and grippy, split by stripes of lichen, and it dries quickly after rain. The cliff feels remote despite a gentle hike of about ten minutes from the trailhead, and the walk in is nicely shaded. Short routes of around 80 feet make it a good half-day outing.

ny_sunshine_city.blurb: Sunshine City is the right-hand end of Spanky's Area, a small crag set among talus beside Route 73 in Chapel Pond Pass. The right side has a handful of good bolted lines, while the left side holds several wandering trad slabs, giving a dozen routes in all. Grades start around 5.4 and reach 5.11, with most in the 5.7 to 5.9 range, so it is a relaxed place to lead bolts or ease into trad. Reach it by dropping down from the pullout, crossing a stream, and following the trail upstream. Black flies can be heavy because of the swamp below.

ny_5_dime_store.blurb: Dime Store is a sector of short, easy-to-moderate climbs within the Rock Dojo top-rope area at Powerlinez. Most of the dozen lines are top-ropes, with a few traditional options including an open-book corner, and no sport routes. The spread runs from a fourth-class scramble through the 5.7 to 5.9 band to a couple of 5.10 lines, so it works well for beginners and groups. Loose rock is a concern, so keep belayers and spectators away from the base. Anchors are trees set back from the edge; the quickest way up is the wide gully at the right end of the sector.

_conflicts.ny_phoenicia_sportsman_s_wall: Stored rock is shale; both pages describe the rock as sandstone (https://www.mountainproject.com/v/109026793, https://www.mountainproject.com/forum/message/111826448).
